source.author: verg
source.text: O mihi praeteritos referat si Iuppiter annos, qualis eram, cum primam aciem Praeneste sub ipsa stravi scutorumque incendi victor acervos et regem hac Erulum dextra sub Tartara misi, nascenti cui tris animas Feronia mater horrendum dictu dederat; terna arma movenda, ter Leto sternendus erat; cui tunc tamen omnis abstulit haec animas dextra et totidem exuit armis:
source.text_original: 'O mihi praeteritos referat si Iuppiter annos, / (qualis eram, cum primam aciem Praeneste sub ipsa / stravi scutorumque incendi victor acervos / et regem hac Erulum dextra sub Tartara misi, / nascenti cui tris animas Feronia mater / (horrendum dictu) dederat; terna arma movenda, / ter Leto sternendus erat; cui tunc tamen omnis / abstulit haec animas dextra et totidem exuit armis: /
source.text_english: O if Jupiter would bring back for me the years gone by, what I was when beneath Praeneste itself I laid low the front line and, victor, burned heaps of shields, and with this right hand sent down to Tartarus their king Erulus, to whom Feronia his mother had given three lives at his birth—horrible to say—three suits of arms had to be overthrown, three times was he to be laid low by death; yet even so this right hand then took from him all his lives and stripped him of just as many suits of armor:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: o si mihi sanguis, quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_original: 'o si mihi sanguis, / quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem / non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, / primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma / concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_english: O if only I had had blood, such as it was when this hand checked Pholus, banner-bearer and threatening with the goblet, not with less gold, I would have been the first to place arms on bronze-clad ships and would have rejoiced to lift the vessel with the shaken oar.
